mainTopic: Limits on public fasts, praying for out-of-season rain, mourning practices during severe fasts, and רבי אלעזר's teachings on public acts of pleading
overview: The amud opens with a story. רבי יהודה נשיאה decreed thirteen fasts (for a calamity other than drought, according to רש"י), and רבי אמי stopped him from adding more so as not to overburden the public. רבי יוחנן rules that the limit applies only to rain, while for other disasters we fast until we are answered. The גמרא explains that this is a מחלוקת between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the reason for the limit. The people of נינוה, who need rain in summer, are told by רבי to ask for it in שומע תפלה, and the הלכה follows this. The גמרא then explains the משנה's rules for the severe fasts. Stores open slightly on Monday and fully on Thursday. Joyful building and planting are cut back. חברים stop greeting one another and sit like mourners. Finally, רבי אלעזר teaches which public acts of pleading, such as falling on one's face, wearing sackcloth or tearing clothes, suit which people, and the verse for his last teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Thirteen fasts decreed with no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה decreed thirteen fasts (for a calamity other than drought, according to רש"י), was not answered, and considered decreeing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He decreed thirteen fasts, but he was not answered. He thought about decreeing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a נשיא who finished thirteen fasts and still was not answered. According to רש"י, these fasts were for some calamity other than drought. This sets up the question of whether he may add more fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's system of fasts for rain ends at thirteen. The נשיא, fasting for a different calamity, wants to go beyond that number. Everything that follows discusses whether this limit is absolute.

phrases.english: He decreed thirteen fasts
phrases.notes: The subject is רבי יהודה נשיאה, from the earlier context.

phrases.english: and he was not answered.
He considered decreeing more.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: after thirteen unanswered fasts, the נשיא wanted to add more.

steps.title: רבי אמי blocks further fasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי tells him not to add fasts, because we do not overburden the public.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said to him: They have said that we do not burden the public too much.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי stops the נשיא from decreeing more fasts. He gives the reason that the public should not be overburdened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי's reason has nothing to do with rain in particular. If the reason is that the public is overburdened, the thirteen-fast limit would apply to any disaster, not only to drought.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said to him:
They have said
one does not trouble the community
excessively.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the נשיא's plan by objecting to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No more than thirteen fasts are decreed, because the public must not be overburdened.

steps.title: רבי אמי was acting on his own view
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says רבי אמי's ruling was his own personal position, not the accepted הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא, son of רבי חייא בר אבא, said: When רבי אמי did this, he did it on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא pushes back against רבי אמי's ruling. He says it was only רבי אמי's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words לגרמיה הוא דעבד mean that רבי אמי did not follow the main view. This weakens his ruling and prepares the way for רבי יוחנן's different rule.

keyTerms.meaning: for himself, on his own opinion

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said:
When Rabbi Ami acted,
he acted on his own authority.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי דַּעֲבַד לְגַרְמֵיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אמי's ruling as a minority personal view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אמי's universal limit of thirteen fasts
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It does not match the main הלכה, which רבי יוחנן reports next.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the limit is only for rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the thirteen-fast limit applies only to rain. For other disasters, we fast until we are answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only for rain. For other kinds of disasters, we keep fasting until Heaven answers.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the הלכה that רבי אבא holds against רבי אמי. The limit on fasts applies only to fasts for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן limits the rule to one situation. For drought, the fasting stops after thirteen days. For other troubles, such as plague or enemies, there is no limit. By this rule, רבי אמי's broad limit was wrong.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה: the thirteen-fast limit is specific to drought. Fasting for other dangers continues until salvation comes.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said as follows,
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They taught this only for rain;
but for other types of calamities,
they continue to fast
until they are answered from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct halacha that replaces רבי אמי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirteen-fast limit applies only to rain. For other calamities, fasting continues until there is an answer.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing: the three and seven fasts were said only about rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: When they said three fasts and when they said seven fasts, they said it only about rain. For other kinds of disasters, we keep fasting until we are answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said. This backs him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed numbers of fasts (three, then three more, then seven, adding up to thirteen) are tied to drought alone. That matches רבי יוחנן's distinction word for word.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
When they said three and when they said seven,
they said it only for rain;
but for other types of calamities,
they continue to fast until they are answered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the limit applies only to rain
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the identical distinction

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רבי אמי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא disproves רבי אמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי אמי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the possibility that רבי אמי has been disproven, since a ברייתא disagrees with him. The next step defends him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbi of the גמרא era (an אמורא) normally cannot argue with a ברייתא. If the ברייתא limits the rule to rain, רבי אמי's general limit would be refuted.

phrases.english: Let us say this is a refutation of Rabbi Ami!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the supporting ברייתא into an attack on רבי אמי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's view that thirteen fasts is the limit for any trouble
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly limits the restriction to rain, and an אמורא cannot argue with a ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי אמי follows one side of a Tannaitic dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי can say that תנאים argue. He follows רבי, who explains the limit as protecting the public from overburden. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains it as the rainy season having passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי can tell you: This is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: We do not decree more than thirteen fasts on the public, because we do not overburden the public. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: That is not the reason. The reason is that the rainy season has already passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אמי. The ברייתא that opposed him represents only one opinion, and there is another תנא who agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, the limit exists to avoid burdening the public, so it applies to every disaster. That is רבי אמי's view. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the limit exists only because fasting for rain after the season is pointless, so it applies only to rain. That is the ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute among תנאים
this is not for that reason
the rainfall that soaks the ground; the rainy season

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the thirteen-fast limit. For רבי, it is not to overburden the public, so it applies to every trouble (רבי אמי's view). For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, it is that the rain season is over, so it applies only to rain (רבי יוחנן's view).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about the number of fasts. Both agree on thirteen. They argue only about the reason, and the reason decides whether the limit applies to disasters other than drought.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami could say to you:
It is a dispute of tanna'im, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹזְרִין יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה תַּעֲנִיּוֹת עַל הַצִּבּוּר,
phrases.english: One does not decree more than thirteen fasts on the community,
because one does not trouble the community
excessively; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
It is not for this reason;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיָּצָא זְמַנָּהּ שֶׁל רְבִיעָה.
phrases.english: rather, it is because the time of the rainfall has passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי אַמֵּי תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the attempted refutation of רבי אמי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: the opposing ברייתא is only one side, and רבי אמי follows the other side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is unanimous, so רבי אמי is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אמי follows רבי, who gives the reason of overburdening the public. The other ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who gives the reason of the rainy season ending.

steps.title: Nineveh asks how to pray for summer rain
steps.stepSummary: The people of נינוה, who need rain even in summer, ask רבי whether they pray for it as individuals or as a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of נינוה sent to רבי: People like us, who need rain even in the season of תמוז, what should we do? Are we like individuals or like a community? Are we like individuals, so we ask in שומע תפלה? Or are we like a community, so we ask in ברכת השנים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A whole city whose climate needs summer rain asks where in the שמונה עשרה to insert their request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The regular request for rain in ברכת השנים follows the calendar of ארץ ישראל and בבל. Individuals with special needs add their requests in שומע תפלה. The question is whether a large city with its own needs counts as a 'community' that may change ברכת השנים.

keyTerms.meaning: the blessing 'Who hears prayer', where private requests are added
the blessing for the year's produce, where rain is requested

phrases.english: The people of Nineveh sent to Rabbi:
People like us, who even in the season of Tammuz
need rain, what should we do?
Are we like individuals or like a community?
Are we like individuals, and so we ask in 'Who listens to prayer',
or are we like a community, and so we ask in the blessing of the years?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new related topic about praying for rain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a whole city with an unusual need for rain is treated as רבים (and changes ברכת השנים) or as יחידים (and asks in שומע תפלה).

steps.title: רבי answers: you are like individuals
steps.stepSummary: רבי rules that the people of נינוה are like individuals and should ask for rain in שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: You are like individuals, and you ask in שומע תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the question. Even a big city does not count as the 'community' for changing ברכת השנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the fixed text of ברכת השנים follows the general seasons of the Jewish world. A single place with special needs, however large, adds its request privately in שומע תפלה.
steps.whatToRemember: A place that needs rain outside the normal season asks for it in שומע תפלה, not in ברכת השנים, because it is treated as individuals.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that communities with different climates add a request for rain in שומע תפלה.

phrases.english: He sent to them:
You are like individuals, and you ask in 'Who listens to prayer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נינוה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are treated as individuals and request rain in שומע תפלה.

steps.title: A teaching from רבי יהודה seems to contradict רבי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי יהודה. It says that nowadays everything depends on local conditions. That seems to mean a place like נינוה asks for rain in ברכת השנים, like a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this. רבי יהודה said: When do these rules about the set times for asking for rain apply? When the years follow their normal pattern and the Jewish people live in their land. But nowadays everything depends on the year, on the place, and on the time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's ruling from the previous step, that the people of נינוה ask for rain as individuals in שומע תפלה. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says the fixed calendar for asking for rain only applies when ארץ ישראל has its normal climate. Today, each place asks for rain according to its own needs. That suggests a place like נינוה would ask in the regular ברכת השנים, as a community, and not only in שומע תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (this is a challenge from a תנאי source)
As they should be (normal, following the usual pattern)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Yehuda said:
When does this apply?
phrases.notes: That is, the fixed times for asking for rain.

phrases.english: At a time when the years are as they should be
and the Jewish people dwell on their land.
But nowadays,
everything depends on the years (the climate),
everything depends on the places,
everything depends on the time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's ruling from Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the people of נינוה ask for rain in שומע תפלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה says that today each place asks for rain according to its local needs. That implies a place like נינוה asks in ברכת השנים as a community, not as individuals.

steps.title: רבי is a תנא and may disagree
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that a ברייתא cannot disprove רבי, because רבי is himself a תנא and may hold differently from רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are challenging רבי with a ברייתא?! רבי is a תנא, and he may disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי is not bound by רבי יהודה's ברייתא, because רבי is also a תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא can disprove an אמורא, who must follow the תנאים. But רבי is at the same level as רבי יהודה. So the two simply disagree, and neither one disproves the other.

keyTerms.meaning: He is a תנא and may disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. 'רבי יהודה' in the ברייתא is a different תנא (רבי יהודה בר אילעי). Do not mix them up.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַתְנִיתָא רָמֵית עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי?!
phrases.english: He said to him: You raise a contradiction from a baraita against Rebbi?!
Rebbi is a tanna, and he may disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה disproves רבי's ruling about נינוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי is a תנא, so he is allowed to disagree with רבי יהודה. His ruling stands as one valid opinion.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since two תנאים disagree, the גמרא asks what the practical conclusion is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the practical bottom line. This line sets up the next step, where אמוראים give their answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know two תנאים disagree, we still need to know which one we follow in practice. Should a place like נינוה ask for rain in ברכת השנים or in שומע תפלה?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical ruling after the disagreement between תנאים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה does a place that needs rain outside the normal season use: ברכת השנים or שומע תפלה?

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says they ask in ברכת השנים, like רבי יהודה. רב ששת says they ask in שומע תפלה, like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In ברכת השנים. רב ששת said: In שומע תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Each one sides with a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן follows רבי יהודה: local need lets them use the regular rain ברכה. רב ששת follows רבי: they count as individuals, so they ask only in the general ברכה for personal requests.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה for the year's produce (בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ), where rain is normally requested
The ברכה 'Who hears prayer', where personal requests may be added

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: In the blessing of the years.
Rav Sheshet said: In 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: ברכת השנים (like רבי יהודה). רב ששת: שומע תפלה (like רבי).

steps.title: The הלכה is: in שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב ששת and רבי. Rain requested outside the normal season is added in שומע תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: in שומע תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling, following רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A place that needs rain when ארץ ישראל does not ask for it in ברכת השנים. Instead, it adds the request in שומע תפלה, like individuals do.
steps.whatToRemember: When a place needs rain outside ארץ ישראל's rainy season, it asks for rain in שומע תפלה, not in ברכת השנים. This follows רבי and רב ששת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical practice of communities whose climate differs from ארץ ישראל: they add the request for rain in שומע תפלה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: in 'Who hears prayer'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions of Step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Rain requested outside the normal season goes in שומע תפלה.

steps.title: The משנה on opening stores Monday and Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: during the stricter fasts, stores open slightly on Monday at dusk, and on Thursday all day, in honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday they open slightly at nightfall, and on Thursday all day, in honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic and quotes a line from the משנה about opening stores during the severe fasts. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the later, stricter public fasts, business is limited as a sign of mourning. The משנה allows some opening on Monday and more on Thursday, so people can buy what they need for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They open slightly (tilt the door partly open)
Because of the honor of שבת

phrases.english: On Monday they open slightly at nightfall
and on Thursday all day
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the stricter fasts, stores open partly on Monday and more on Thursday, in honor of שבת.

steps.title: How should the משנה be read?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reading is right. Option one: on Thursday they also open only slightly, but all day. Option two: on Monday they open slightly, and on Thursday they open fully all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: How is it taught? Is it: 'On Monday they open slightly at nightfall, and on Thursday (slightly) all day, in honor of שבת'? Or perhaps: 'On Monday they open slightly, and on Thursday they open fully all day'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה's words really mean. It offers two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, the word מטין (slightly) applies to both days, and Thursday only adds more hours. In the second reading, Monday allows slight opening, and Thursday allows a fully open door all day. The question is whether Thursday's leniency is about more hours or about opening the door wider.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a dilemma the גמרא then tries to settle)
How is it taught? (how do we read the words?)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the difference between מטין (open just a little) and פותחין (open fully). The whole question depends on these two words.

phrases.english: It was asked of them: How is it taught?
'On Monday they open slightly at nightfall,'
'and on Thursday (slightly) all day,'
'because of the honor of Shabbat'?
Or perhaps: 'On Monday they open slightly (all day),'
'and on Thursday they open fully the entire day'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the משנה quoted in Step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does Thursday allow slight opening for more hours, or full opening all day?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows Thursday means fully open
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says: on Monday they open slightly until evening, and on Thursday they open fully the whole day. This supports the second reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught in a ברייתא: On Monday they open slightly until evening, and on Thursday they open fully the entire day, in honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא that spells out the rule clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word פותחין (fully open) for Thursday, so the second reading is correct. Monday allows slight opening for the whole day, until evening. Thursday allows full opening, because people need to shop for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source that answers the question)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught in a baraita:
On Monday they open slightly until the evening,
and on Thursday they open fully the entire day
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of Step 16 using a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second reading is correct: on Monday they open slightly all day, and on Thursday they open fully all day.

steps.title: Rules for two doors or a blocking platform
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds two details. A shop with two doors opens one and keeps the other locked. If a platform blocks the view of the door, the owner may open normally.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had two doors, he opens one and locks one. If he had a platform in front of his door, he opens as usual and does not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with practical cases about how a store owner shows he is limiting business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is that the store should not look like it is running normally on a day of mourning. With two doors, locking one shows restraint. If a platform already hides the door from the street, no one will notice the opening, so there is no concern.

keyTerms.meaning: A platform or bench (blocking the doorway from view)

steps.whatToRemember: During the stricter fasts, stores open only slightly on Monday and fully on Thursday, for שבת needs. The aim is that business should not look normal, which is why a shop with two doors opens one and locks one.

phrases.english: If he had two entrances,
he opens one and locks one.
If he had a platform opposite his entrance,
he opens in his usual way and need not be concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with practical details
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two doors, open one and lock one. If a platform hides the door, open normally.

steps.title: If the fasts pass unanswered, business, building and planting are reduced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if these fasts pass with no answer, people cut back on business, building and planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: If these fasts passed and they were not answered, they cut back on business, on building, and on planting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה so that it can explain it. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the משנה listed the fasts themselves. Now it adds limits on normal daily life, because the drought is still going on. The words 'building' and 'planting' are unclear, and the next step will define them.

phrases.english: If these passed and they were not answered —
they cut back on business,
phrases.notes: 'Taking and giving' is the phrase for doing business.

phrases.english: on building and on planting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the stores on Monday and Thursday to the משנה's next set of limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the stricter fasts pass unanswered, people reduce business, building and planting.

steps.title: Only joyful building and planting are reduced
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the משנה means only building and planting done for joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'Building' means building for joy. 'Planting' means planting for joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that narrows the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this ברייתא you might think all building and planting must slow down. The ברייתא limits the rule to building and planting done for joy, not for basic needs. People still need homes and food, but celebration does not fit a time of drought.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think all building and planting is cut back. Only joyful building and planting are reduced, as the next step explains.

phrases.english: It was taught: 'building' — building for joy.
'Planting' — planting for joy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the words 'building' and 'planting' from the משנה quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The limit applies only to building and planting done for joy.

steps.title: Examples: a wedding house and a royal garden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives an example of each. Joyful building is a wedding house for one's son. Joyful planting is a fancy royal-style garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is building for joy? This is one who builds a wedding house for his son. What is planting for joy? This is one who plants a fancy garden like kings have.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives a clear example of 'joyful' building and of 'joyful' planting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wedding house was a small home built for a son's wedding feast and for the new couple to live in at first. The royal garden is planted only for beauty, not for food. Both are luxuries of celebration, so they are cut back during a drought.

keyTerms.meaning: A wedding house built for a son
A fancy, kingly garden planted for beauty

phrases.english: What is building for joy —
this is one who builds a wedding house for his son.

phrases.aramaic: אִי זוֹ הִיא נְטִיעָה שֶׁל שִׂמְחָה —
phrases.english: What is planting for joy —
this is one who plants a fancy garden like kings have.
phrases.notes: A garden only for beauty and pleasure, not for food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of the 'joyful' building and planting named in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joyful building is a wedding house for a son. Joyful planting is a royal decorative garden.

steps.title: The משנה also reduces greetings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another phrase from the משנה: greetings are also reduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in greeting one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, which says people also reduce greetings. This sets up the ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase continues the משנה's list of things that are reduced. It does not explain how greetings are reduced, so the גמרא brings a ברייתא next.

phrases.english: And in greeting one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds greetings to the list of things reduced in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the stricter fasts, greetings are reduced.

steps.title: חברים do not greet, and answer עמי הארץ quietly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חברים do not greet one another at all. If an עם הארץ greets them, they answer softly and seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: חברים do not greet one another at all. If עמי הארץ greet them, they answer in a low voice and in a serious way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains how greetings are reduced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חברים are careful about מצוות, so they stop greeting one another completely. An עם הארץ who does not know this rule may still greet them. They do not ignore him, because that would insult him. Instead they answer in a quiet and serious way, which shows that this is a sad time.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are very careful about מצוות

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Among חברים, there is no greeting between them.
עמי הארץ who greet them —
phrases.notes: They do not know the rule.

phrases.english: they answer them in a low voice,
and in a serious way.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲבֵרִים, אֵין שְׁאֵילַת שָׁלוֹם בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the greeting limit from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חברים do not greet one another. They answer the greetings of עמי הארץ softly and seriously.

steps.title: Sitting like mourners until Heaven has mercy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the חברים wrap themselves and sit like mourners, like people pushed away by ה׳, until Heaven shows mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they wrap themselves and sit like mourners and like people in נידוי, like people rebuked by ה׳, until Heaven has mercy on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא finishes by describing the mood the people take on while the drought continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares them to אבלים and to people in נידוי, who are kept apart from others. The point is that the drought is a sign ה׳ is displeased, so people act humbled. This lasts until the rain comes.

keyTerms.meaning: People in נידוי (kept apart from the community)

steps.whatToRemember: When the fasts pass with no rain, daily life becomes like mourning: less business, no joyful building or planting, almost no greetings, and people sit like אבלים until Heaven has mercy.

phrases.english: And they wrap themselves and sit
like mourners and like people in נידוי,
like people rebuked by ה׳,
phrases.notes: 'The Place' (המקום) is a name for ה׳.

phrases.english: until Heaven has mercy on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 23 with the overall mourning behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People sit wrapped like mourners until Heaven shows mercy.

steps.title: An important person may not fall on his face unless sure to be answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that an אדם חשוב may not fall on his face in public prayer unless he will be answered like יהושע בן נון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: An important person may not fall on his face unless he will be answered like יהושע בן נון, as the verse says: 'And ה׳ said to יהושע: Get up! Why are you falling on your face?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר about public acts of prayer, which fits the topic of fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an important person throws himself on his face in public and is not answered, people may mock him, and that shames him. So he should do this only if he is confident he will be answered. The proof is יהושע, who fell on his face and was answered right away by ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: To fall on his face (lie down in prayer)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the idea that an אדם חשוב must be careful with public acts of prayer, so that his honor is not hurt if he is not answered.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לִיפּוֹל עַל פָּנָיו,
phrases.english: An important person is not allowed to fall on his face,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נַעֲנֶה כִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן,
phrases.english: unless he will be answered like יהושע בן נון,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קֻם לָךְ
phrases.english: as it says: 'And Hashem said to יהושע: Get up,'

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה זֶּה אַתָּה נֹפֵל עַל פָּנֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: 'why are you falling on your face?'
phrases.notes: יהושע ז:י. יהושע fell on his face and was answered right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לִיפּוֹל עַל פָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the community's behavior to a new teaching about an individual leader's public prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אדם חשוב may fall on his face in public only if he is sure to be answered, like יהושע.

steps.title: An important person may not wear sackcloth unless sure to be answered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר also teaches that an אדם חשוב may not wear sackcloth unless he will be answered like יהורם בן אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: An important person may not put on sackcloth unless he will be answered like יהורם בן אחאב, as the verse says: 'When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes. He was walking on the wall, and the people saw, and there was the sackcloth on his body.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching of רבי אלעזר that follows the same pattern as the first, this time about sackcloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sackcloth is a public sign of mourning and pleading with ה׳. The reasoning is the same as before: an important person should not do this unless he will be answered. The proof is יהורם בן אחאב, who wore sackcloth during the siege and was answered when the siege ended, even though he was a wicked king.

keyTerms.meaning: To put on sackcloth (rough mourning clothing)
King of ישראל during the siege of שומרון

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's two rules match: an אדם חשוב should not fall on his face or wear sackcloth in public unless he is sure to be answered, like יהושע and like יהורם.

phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לַחֲגוֹר שַׂק
phrases.english: An important person is not allowed to put on sackcloth

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נַעֲנֶה כִּיהוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב,
phrases.english: unless he will be answered like יהורם בן אחאב,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי כִשְׁמֹעַ הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת דִּבְרֵי הָאִשָּׁה
phrases.english: as it says: 'And when the king heard the woman's words,'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ו:ל, during the terrible famine in the siege of שומרון.

phrases.aramaic: וַיִּקְרַע אֶת בְּגָדָיו וְהוּא עֹבֵר עַל הַחֹמָה
phrases.english: 'he tore his clothes, and he was walking on the wall,'

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּרְא הָעָם וְהִנֵּה הַשַּׂק עַל בְּשָׂרוֹ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: 'and the people saw, and there was the sackcloth on his body,' and so on.
phrases.notes: The siege was later lifted, so he was answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין אָדָם חָשׁוּב רַשַּׁאי לַחֲגוֹר שַׂק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי אלעזר, built the same way as step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אדם חשוב may wear sackcloth in public only if he is sure to be answered, like יהורם בן אחאב.

steps.title: Not everyone prays by tearing, not everyone by falling
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that משה and אהרן prayed by falling on their faces, while יהושע and כלב prayed by tearing their clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Not everyone uses tearing, and not everyone uses falling. משה and אהרן used falling. יהושע and כלב used tearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי אלעזר. Like his last two statements, it is about which public acts of pleading suit which people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling on one's face (נפילת אפים) is treated as a higher form of pleading than tearing clothes (קריעה). The greater leaders, משה and אהרן, fell on their faces. Their students, יהושע and כלב, only tore their garments. This fits רבי אלעזר's theme that some acts of prayer suit only people on a certain level.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's clothes, as a sign of pain and pleading
Falling on one's face in prayer

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Not everyone is with tearing (of garments)
and not everyone is with falling (on the face).
Moses and Aaron: with falling,
Joshua and Caleb: with tearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הַכֹּל בִּקְרִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third statement of רבי אלעזר in the same series about what fits a person's stature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Falling on the face fits the greatest leaders (משה and אהרן). Tearing garments fits the next level (יהושע and כלב).

steps.title: Proof from the verses in the spies story
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר proves his teaching from two back-to-back פסוקים in פרשת שלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה and אהרן used falling, as it is written: 'And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces.' יהושע and כלב used tearing, as it is written: 'And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh tore their clothes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where in the תורה we see each pair doing its act. These פסוקים come right after the spies' bad report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says only that משה and אהרן fell. The next פסוק says only that יהושע and כלב tore their clothes. רבי אלעזר reads this as a split: each pair did a different act, matching its level.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Moses and Aaron with falling, as it is written:
'And Moses and Aaron fell on their faces' (Numbers 14:5).
phrases.notes: Said in response to the spies' report.

phrases.english: Joshua and Caleb with tearing, as it is written:
'And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh
tore their garments' (Numbers 14:6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural basis for the split in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that משה and אהרן fell on their faces while יהושע and כלב only tore their clothes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר יד:ה-ו, two פסוקים in a row that describe each pair doing a different act.

steps.title: The extra letter ו shows Joshua and Caleb did both
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני) objects: the word 'וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ' (AND Joshua) shows that יהושע and כלב also fell, and then tore as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged this, and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני: If the פסוק had said 'Joshua', it would be as you say. Now that it says 'AND Joshua', they did this and that.
steps.whatsHappening: A later חכם attacks רבי אלעזר's reading of the פסוק. He says the פסוק does not prove that יהושע and כלב only tore their clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ו ('and') links the second פסוק to the first. It can mean: 'and also יהושע and כלב', so they joined in the falling and added tearing on top. If so, the פסוקים do not show that falling was kept only for משה and אהרן. The proof for רבי אלעזר's split is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another name for the same speaker)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not saying that יהושע and כלב did NOT tear their clothes. It says they did BOTH, falling and tearing. So the פסוק cannot prove they were only fit for tearing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to it,
and some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani:
If it had been written 'Joshua', it would be as you say;
now that it is written 'And Joshua',
he did this and that (both falling and tearing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading that the פסוקים show יהושע and כלב only tore their clothes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The connecting ו in 'וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ' adds יהושע and כלב to the falling in the earlier פסוק. So they did both acts, and the split between the pairs is not proven.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר splits the acts by level: falling for משה and אהרן, tearing for יהושע and כלב. רבי זירא answers that the ו in 'וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ' can mean יהושע and כלב did both.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one small letter in a פסוק can undo a whole proof.

steps.title: Kings will stand and ministers will bow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that not everyone honors ה׳ by standing up, and not everyone by bowing: kings will stand and ministers will bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Not everyone is with rising, and not everyone is with bowing. Kings are with rising, and ministers are with bowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אלעזר in the same 'not everyone' style. This time it is about how great people will honor ה׳ in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching follows the same pattern: different people show respect in different ways, based on their rank. For a king, even standing up is a big act of honor. Ministers, who are lower, show honor by bowing all the way down.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Not everyone is with rising
and not everyone is with bowing.
Kings: with rising,
and ministers: with bowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא הַכֹּל בְּקִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another רבי אלעזר teaching built on the same 'not everyone' pattern as step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, kings will honor ה׳ by standing and ministers by bowing.

steps.title: The verse proof for kings rising begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a פסוק from ישעיהו to prove that kings will honor ה׳ by standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kings with rising, as it is written: 'Thus says ה׳, the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to bring the proof for the kings' part of the teaching. The פסוק is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from ישעיהו מט:ז. The words about kings seeing and rising come later in the פסוק. So far only the opening words appear, which set up the proof.

phrases.english: Kings with rising, as it is written:
'Thus says the Lord, the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו מט:ז. The פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the scriptural support for step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that kings will honor ה׳ by standing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו מט:ז. Only the opening is quoted here, and the proof words come on the next amud.
